channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: Lions RT Blake Miller (knee) is not on the injury report for Week 3 against the Jets.
item.description:
Blake Miller DET Tackle

Lions LG Christian Mahogany (hip) will also make his return after a week-long absence, and RG Tate Ratledge (elbow) is good to go after two limited sessions early in the week. The Lions’ starting offensive line’s health is improving. Backup OG Ben Bartch (foot) has been ruled out.

Source: Detroit Lions

item.title: Chiefs DT Chris Jones (calf) is not on the injury report for Week 3 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Chris Jones KC Defensive Tackle

The Chiefs kept Jones limited in all three practices this week, so this injury isn’t totally behind him yet. Regardless, he should have a productive day against the Dolphins’ offense this week.

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said “it seems like” 49ers WR Mike Evans (hip) “has a pretty good chance” to play in Week 3 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Rapoport made the statement, and then immediately referenced 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan’s comments earlier this week, when he said Evans had a “good” chance to play this week, so it is unclear if Rapoport is actually breaking news. That said, no news is good news. If the NFL Network star had learned something contradictory, we would have heard about it. Evans returned to practice in a limited capacity today. Stay tuned for updates and treat him as a WR2 for the time being.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Commanders QB Jayden Daniels (elbow) is unlikely to play in Week 4 against the Colts.
item.description:
Jayden Daniels WAS Quarterback

Frankly, this report comes off as more of a recap than breaking news. The Commanders do not yet know when Daniels will return, though they are optimistic that he will miss fewer than four games. According to Rapoport, the goal is to get him back “as soon as possible” and “as safe as possible.” Backup QB

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Vikings RB DeeJay Dallas (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
DeeJay Dallas MIN Running Back

Dallas and starting RB Aaron Jones (knee) both practiced in full on Friday. Jones will handle the majority of the backfield’s touches while Dallas takes a few carries and plays some on passing downs.

item.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) will miss multiple weeks.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive End

Bosa strained his calf while going through his pre-practice warm-up routine on Thursday. The team has not yet identified Bosa’s expected return timeline, but the 49ers’ pass rusher will be out for some time. The 49ers also ruled out EDGE Romello Height (hand) for Week 3 against the Cardinals as well.

Source: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk

item.title: Dolphins WR Chris Bell (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

Bell upgraded to full participation on Friday after two limited sessions. The rookie wide receiver has been bothered by fluid and soreness in his surgically repaired knee since Week 1, so the Dolphins have limited his snaps in-game. With fellow rookie WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) sidelined for Week 3, the coaching staff could draw up a couple of extra plays with Bell in mind, though he can only be viewed as a WR4.

Source: Miami Dolphins

item.title: MarShawn Lloyd played on 22.7 percent of the offensive snaps in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
item.description:
MarShawn Lloyd GB Running Back

The Packers largely played in a trailing game script last night. Lloyd does not have meaningful access to passing down snaps, logging just one snap on third down and none in the two-minute drill, making him mostly dependent on decent rushing workloads. He played 45.5 percent of the red zone snaps and took the lone snap inside the five-yard line, but was held out of the end zone. Lloyd’s six touches led the backfield, but are hardly enough to keep him locked in 12-team FLEX spots.

item.title: Eagles WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) resumed practicing on Friday.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Smith was back at practice, logging a limited session, after sitting out yesterday. The Eagles’ WR1 is on track to play, but hamstring injuries can be finicky. This is worth tracking closely. The Bears have fielded a very fantasy-friendly pass defense thus far, making this a favorable matchup for the Eagles’ passing attack.

Source: Zack Berman

item.title: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley (stinger) practiced in full on Friday.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley told reporters after practice that he is confident in his rehab program and plans to play in Week 3 against the Bears. His backups, RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and RB Will Shipley (foot), both resumed practicing today as limited participants. Expect Barkley to handle his normal workload in what should be a run-heavy game plan.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson is set to handle No. 2 pass-catcher duties with WR Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined this week. The young tight end posted a 6/54/1 receiving line in Week 2 and can be viewed as a TE1 in this matchup.

Source: Sarah Barshop

item.title: Cardinals qB Jacoby Brissett (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Jacoby Brissett ARI Quarterback

Brissett practiced fully all week, despite the hip injury. Brissett is not quite hitting the peaks he produced last year and is too tough to trust in 12-team leagues. Consider him a QB2 against the 49ers this week.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (Achilles) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Garrett Williams ARI Cornerback

The Cardinals lost their top perimeter CB Will Johnson (neck) to injured reserve this week. Fellow perimeter CB Max Melton (toe) is questionable to play. Williams suffered a season-ending Achilles tendon rupture last year, and returns this week to man the slot.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (stinger/foot) is doubtful for Week 3 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

Wright was unable to practice on Friday. He is very unlikely to play, although his absence may only be felt in the return game. Dolphins RB

Source: Miami Dolphins

item.title: 49ers ruled out WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) for Week 3 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Demarcus Robinson SF Wide Receiver

This was the expected outcome for Week 3. Reports on Robinson’s injury indicate this could be a multi-week issue. With WR1 Mike Evans (hip) questionable, WR Deebo Samuel and TE George Kittle could take on sizable workloads, though the team will likely still try to limit Kittle’s snap count.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans (hip) is questionable to play in Week 3 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was in uniform and warming up during the open portion of Friday’s practice. When asked whether Evans was limited or full, he declined to say. If Evans was full, we have almost no concerns about his ability to play this week, though he likely would have been removed from the injury report if that were the case. Evans must be treated as truly questionable to play, so make a backup plan, but he is the type of player who does not necessarily need to practice fully before practicing. If active, he is a WR2.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Bears K Cairo Santos (right hip) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Cairo Santos CHI Kicker

Santos has tumbled from the potential beneficiary of a potent offense to a droppable player in 12-team leagues. He is also on the wrong side of questionable.

Source: Dan Wiederer

item.title: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Cooper Kupp SEA Wide Receiver

Kupp will be available for QB Sam Darnold (glute), who makes his return from his Week 1 injury. Kupp is a mild FLEX option, facing a soft Commanders’ coverage unit.

Source: John P. Boyle

item.title: Commanders S Nick Cross (illness) won’t play in Washington’s Week 3 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Nick Cross WAS Safety

He didn’t practice all week after spending Sunday night in a Dallas hospital following an “internal injury” he suffered against the Cowboys. Sounds ominous. We’d be unsurprised if Cross were placed on injured reserve on Saturday.

item.title: Seahawks ruled out S Julian Love (calf) for Week 3 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Julian Love SEA Safety

The Seahawks also ruled out S Ty Okada (hamstring) for this week’s game. Okada has not yet played in 2026. Love injured his calf in practice this week. The Seahawks’ D/ST remains a worthwhile play against the Commanders, thanks to the defense’s overall talent and coach Mike Macdonald’s top-tier scheming. Losing the two safeties will simply complicate Macdonald’s preferred three-safety looks.

Source: John P. Boyle

item.title: Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw (back/shoulder) is not on Washington’s final Week 3 injury report.
item.description:
Javon Kinlaw WAS Defensive Tackle

He was limited on Thursday and practiced in full today to avoid the questionable line. The 28-year-old defensive tackle can look forward to a Sunday of trying to stop Jadarian Price runs right up the gut.

item.title: Commanders G Sam Cosmi (concussion, throat) will not play in Washington’s Week 3 game against Seattle.
item.description:
Sam Cosmi WAS OFFENSIVE GUARD (SUB)

He did not practice at any point this week and should be regarded as questionable for Week 4. The Commanders are without their two best offensive linemen, which should make life very interesting (in a bad way) for Marcus Mariota in Week 3.

item.title: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) will not play in Washington’s Week 3 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo has yet to practice after getting injured in Week 1, leading some to wonder if the Commanders know that there’s an injured reserve list they can place players on. Ben Sinnott has filled in for Okonkwo; Sinnott can best be viewed in his natural habitat on the waiver wire as he scores 1.6 points this week.

item.title: Kaytron Allen (hip) is not on Washington’s final Week 3 injury report.
item.description:
Kaytron Allen WAS Running Back

Allen will be available for third-string running back duties against the Seahawks, and considering the likelihood the Commanders are blown out, stands some chance at scoring about 1-3 fantasy points.

item.title: Marvin Mims (foot) is questionable for Denver’s Week 3 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Marvin Mims DEN Wide Receiver

Mims re-aggravated his preseason foot injury in Week 1 and did not play in Week 2. He was able to get three limited sessions in ahead of Week 3, but has no fantasy value at this point in Denver’s deep wideout room. He’d provide considerable real-life value as a punt returner.

item.title: Seahawks RB Jadarian Price (chest) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Price’s injury responded well to treatment this week. The rookie running back got “a ton of reps” in practices and is reportedly ready to be “full go” against the Commanders on Sunday. Price is a low-end RB2/FLEX for the occasion, after splitting carries with RB Emanuel Wilson and ceding passing down reps to RB George Holani (knee) in Week 2.

Source: Gregg Bell

item.title: Jonah Coleman (ankle) won’t play in Denver’s Week 3 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

For sale: one large FAAB bid, never used.

item.title: RJ Harvey (hamstring) is not on Denver’s final Week 3 injury report.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

He’ll hold the receiving end of Denver’s RB tandem in Week 3 against the Broncos, giving him fringe RB2 status against a tough defense. We’d probably rather start Harvey than committee mate J.K. Dobbins this week with Jonah Coleman (ankle) out.

item.title: J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) is not on Denver’s final Week 3 injury report.
item.description:
J.K. Dobbins DEN Running Back

He’ll form a committee with RJ Harvey, who was also cleared for Week 3, against the Rams. Dobbins is a low-end RB2 at best in this role against a tough Los Angeles defense.

item.title: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Darnold upgraded to full participation yesterday, so today’s news tracks. In an interview on the Rich Eisen Show earlier today, Seahawks WR Smith-Njigba basically let slip that Darnold would be back, but Eisen let him out of the situation with only a soft follow-up. Darnold can be started as a borderline QB1/2 against a fantasy-friendly Commanders defense in Week 3.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Jets ruled out S Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) for Week 3 against the Lions.
item.description:
Minkah Fitzpatrick NYJ Safety

Fitzpatrick did not practice at all this week. Starting EDGE Joseph Ossai (foot) is questionable to play, though rookie EDGE David Bailey (elbow) is good to go. This looks like a potentially high-scoring game.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: Jets WR Adonai Mitchell (finger) is questionable to play in Week 3 against the Lions.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Mitchell got his finger caught in a jersey on Thursday, but he shared no further details. ESPN’s Rich Cimini reported that there is “some concern” regarding the injury, and Mitchell was seen practicing with some sort of all-encompassing wrap around his hand, index finger and middle finger. The speedy wide receiver is firmly in the questionable camp. If active, he must be viewed as a boom-bust WR3/FLEX, though this matchup against the Lions is very favorable.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: Chiefs LT Josh Simmons (back) will not play in Kansas City’s Week 3 game against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Josh Simmons KC Tackle

Kahlil Benson draws another start. Simmons has not been spotted at practice since the regular season started.

item.title: Malik Nabers is not on New York’s final Week 3 injury report.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

It sure didn’t seem like he had great chemistry with Jameis Winston on Monday night, leaving Nabers feeling more like a mid-range WR2 than someone you’d really want to count on to carry you to victory in what will be a windy Week 3 game against the Titans. Still, he’s fully healthy and got in full practices in each of the last two days of the week to clear the injury report.

item.title: Giants EDGE Brian Burks is questionable for New York’s Week 3 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Brian Burns NYG Outside Linebacker

It feels like an aggressive questionable as Burns officially missed all three days of practice this week, but it’s likely a good sign for his availability for Week 4. Joining Burns as questionable are CB Deonte Banks (calf) and S Tyler Nubin (calf) as the Giants try to right the ship with Jameis Winston under center.

item.title: Ravens LT Ronnie Stanley (toe) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 3 game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Ronnie Stanley BAL Tackle

Stanley didn’t practice at any point this week and is clearly worse off than he was last week, when he at least made it to the questionable line. Carson Vinson replaced Stanley towards the end of Baltimore’s Week 2 loss to the Saints and would seem to be the fill-in.

item.title: Trey Hendrickson (finger) isn’t on Baltimore’s final Week 3 injury report.
item.description:
Trey Hendrickson BAL Outside Linebacker

Questionable with this ailment last week, Hendrickson played in Week 2 with a cast. It seems like that will be the plan going forward. Hendrickson got in a full session today. Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) was also not on the injury report and is slated to make his season debut in Week 3.

item.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 3 game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter was vaguely optimistic about Flowers’ status when asked; Flowers returned in a limited session as the Ravens did a walkthrough. This will be one to monitor on Sunday, but Flowers is probably still on the pessimistic side of questionable at the moment.

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) isn’t on Jacksonville’s final injury report for Week 3.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

He will play against the Patriots. Meyers got in his first full practice since suffering the thumb injury and should be a reasonable FLEX play against New England.

item.title: Texans RT Trent Brown (knee/wrist) is questionable for Week 3 against the Colts.
item.description:
Trent Brown HOU Tackle

The Texans ruled out RG Ed Ingram (groin) and EDGE Jadevon Clowney (knee). The Colts’ defense has played unimpressively thus far, but hopefully Brown is able to play this week. Losing two offensive line starters is less than ideal.

Source: Houston Texans

item.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. (nir/conditioning) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 3 game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

He was limited all three days this week and expressed uncertainty about his status for the game when asked on Thursday. He’s best regarded as a true game-time decision; the Steelers would surely like to have him on deck against Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase. Joining Porter on the questionable line is fellow CB Jamel Dean (ankle), who was limited the last two practices of the week after missing Wednesday.

item.title: Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 3 game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

He was limited in practice all three days this week with a foot injury that kept him out of Week 2. We’d say Pittman is on the optimistic side of questionable based on his participation status. If he’s out again, it would likely be Germie Bernard picking up the slack, as he did in Week 2.

item.title: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 3 game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Jaylen Warren PIT Running Back

Warren got in three limited practices this week and, given Rico Dowdle was already ruled out, feels likely to be active on Sunday. Warren will get a workload boost if he can handle it. Eli Heidenreich, Pittsburgh’s seventh-round pick, is next on the depth chart behind Warren with Dowdle out.

item.title: Texans ruled out WR Nico Collins (hamstring) for Week 3 against the Colts.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

Collins will miss his second consecutive game with yet another hamstring strain. Last week, the passing offense ran through TE Dalton Schultz, who earned 13 targets. Fellow Texans WR Xavier Hutchinson was next with eight targets, but he caught just three, making for a shaky FLEX option this week.

Source: Houston Texans

item.title: Rico Dowdle (toe) will not play in Pittsburgh’s Week 3 game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Dowdle didn’t practice at any point this week with a toe injury that was described by Ian Rapoport as a “day-to-day” issue after Week 2. It sounds like he enters Week 4 as very much questionable. 2026 seventh-rounder Eli Heidenreich will likely back up Jaylen Warren on Sunday.

item.title: Bears QB Tyson Bagent (concussion) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Tyson Bagent CHI Quarterback

Bagent will almost certainly be ruled out for the Bears’ Week 3 Monday Night Football game against the Eagles, paving the way for his backup, QB Case Keenum, to get the start.

Source: Sean Hammond

item.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

This is expected, but the Bears have not officially ruled out Williams, so we will continue to provide updates. According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Williams is not expected to play in Week 3’s Monday Night Football game against the Eagles. Bears QB3 Case Keenum is currently in line to start.

Source: Sean Hammond

item.title: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 3 game against the Giants.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

He did return for a limited session on Friday, but it doesn’t look like it’s a sure thing he plays in Week 3. Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Nick Singleton could get more opportunities in Week 3.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: Kyle Monangai (knee) returned to practice in full on Friday.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

It doesn’t seem like there’s much concern that he’ll miss Monday Night’s game against the Eagles after skipping the first practice of the week for the team on Thursday. Monangai took two limited sessions with a different ailment (hamstring) last week and should be in line for RB2 duties behind D’Andre Swift in what could be a more limited Bears running game with Case Keenum under center.

Source: Brad Biggs

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Kaye believes AJ Dillon could spell Chuba Hubbard on “obvious passing downs” in Week 3.
item.description:
AJ Dillon CAR Running Back

Dillon will step into the main backup role for Week 3 after Jonathon Brooks (groin) wound up on injured reserve. There’s no real timeshare here; Hubbard will be the main back. But Dillon could cut into PPR point territory as Panthers OC Brad Idzik was described as “pleasantly surprised” by the veteran’s receiving ability.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Eagles RB Will Shipley (foot) resumed practicing on Friday.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

Shipley now has a chance to suit up on Monday night against the Bears. With starting RB Saquon Barkley (stinger) and RB2 Tank Bigsby (abdomen) also practicing, Shipley may not get any work, even if he is active.

Source: Brooks Kubena

item.title: Brock Bowers (knee) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 3 game against the Saints.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers did not practice today, but head coach Klint Kubiak said that was part of the team’s plan for managing his injury. Bowers had been limited each of the past two days. It seems plausible given how often he’s being managed at practice that he’d be on a snap count if active, but that’s just our speculation. Kubiak added that the team will not be working Bowers out pre-game like they did ahead of Week 2. Bowers-reliant managers are used to having contingency plans at this point and that will remain the case for Week 3.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Eagles RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) resumed practicing on Friday.
item.description:
Tank Bigsby PHI Running Back

Bigsby is tentatively on track to be available for backup duties in the Eagles’ Monday Night Football game against the Bears. Starting RB Saquon Barkley (stinger) continues to practice, so he should be good to go for his regular workload.

Source: Brooks Kubena

item.title: Vikings RB Aaron Jones (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Aaron Jones MIN Running Back

Jones, 33, sat out on Wednesday before returning to practice on Thursday. He tweaked his knee in Week 2, but it is not going to sideline him this week. Vikings receiving specialist RB DeeJay Dallas will rotate in behind him, but is unlikely to warrant PPR FLEX consideration. Rookie RB Demond Claiborne is only a bench stash. Jones can be treated as a low-end RB2/FLEX.

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: Kendre Miller (illness) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 3 injury report.
item.description:
Kendre Miller NO Running Back

He returned to practice today and practiced in full after missing Thursday to an illness. That’s not exactly a guarantee he’ll play; he was a healthy scratch last week behind Alvin Kamara.

item.title: Giants T Andrew Thomas (groin) said he’ll play in New York’s Week 3 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

Players aren’t always the most reliable source and Thomas may still be listed as questionable, but Thomas did practice in full today per John Harbaugh. The Giants star left tackle will protect Jameis Winston against the Titans.

Source: Dan Duggan

item.title: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (quad) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Jordan Whittington

Whittington is WR Puka Nacua’s (hip) direct backup, so he will be out there running a decent number of routes. Whittington has, however, never managed to establish himself as a reliable contributor. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. Rams TE Colby Parkinson (knee) will be questionable.

Source: Stu Jackson

item.title: Saints ruled out WR Barion Brown (hamstring) for Week 3 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Barion Brown NO Wide Receiver

The Saints will be without their gadget wide receiver and return specialist. His absence should allow WR Bryce Lance to consolidate routes in the No. 3 wide receiver role, but Lance is only a 14-team dart throw. Hopefully, Brown is back at it next week.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Travis Etienne NO Running Back

We do not yet know today’s participation level, but Etienne logged two limited sessions to begin the week. Hopefully, we get a report pre-game revealing the injury’s severity, so we can better assess his potential usage. Given the Saints’ prior backfield workload splits and Etienne’s soft-tissue strain, he should probably be viewed as a low-end RB2/FLEX starter right now.

Source: Ross Jackson

item.title: Ty Johnson (hamstring) is not on Buffalo’s final Week 3 injury report.
item.description:
Ty Johnson BUF Running Back

He practiced in full all week and will return to his third-down role against the Chargers.

item.title: Brenen Thompson (quad) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 3 game against the Bills.
item.description:
Brenen Thompson LAC Wide Receiver

He didn’t practice at any point this week and should be regarded as questionable for Week 4 at this time. Thompson played just 22 snaps in LA’s first two games, so his absence won’t necessarily free up more snaps for anyone else.

item.title: Chargers G Trey Pipkins (knee) and Kayode Awosika (fibula) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 3 game against the Bills.
item.description:
Trey Pipkins LAC Tackle

Rashawn Slater (groin) and Cole Strange (pectoral) were removed from the injury report on Friday. The end result of these moves will likely be Trevor Penning starting at guard. Nobody ever said life was easy for Justin Herbert.

item.title: Ladd McConkey (ribs) is not on Los Angeles’ final injury report for Week 3 against the Bills.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

He practiced in full all week and will presumably be more involved than he was in Week 2, when he was on a snap count. McConkey can be started as a mid-range WR2 despite Los Angeles’ struggles so far against a Bills defense that has allowed 30 points in each of their first two games.

item.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) returned to practice on Friday.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Baltimore Banner’s Jonas Shaffer maintained the beat’s skepticism of Flowers’ availability for Week 3’s game in Rio by saying it “still seems unlikely” he’ll play. At the very least, Flowers’ appearance is probably a good sign for his chance for Week 4. We’ll grab a fresh update once the Ravens drop statuses; it seems likely Flowers will not be better than questionable.

Source: Jonas Shaffer

item.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua (hip) is doubtful to play in Week 3 against the Broncos, but should play in Week 4 against the Eagles, barring a setback.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua will not practice today, either. The bad news comes straight from Rams coach Sean McVay. With Nacua sidelined, WR Davante Adams must be treated as a fantasy football WR1 and TE Terrance Ferguson can be expected to operate as the team’s No. 2 pass catcher. He is a worthwhile TE1 starter.

Source: Stu Jackson

item.title: Ed Oliver (hip) is questionable for Week 3 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Ed Oliver BUF Defensive Lineman

Oliver was a surprise scratch in last week’s game against the Lions after suffering an injury in pre-game warmups. It was reported on Sunday that Oliver was day-to-day with “a chance” to play against the Chargers. After being limited in back-to-back practice to close out the week, it’s fair to assume he’ll have a chance to suit up on Sunday barring any setbacks.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Bills coach Joe Brady said Keon Coleman (ankle) is questionable and will be a game-time decision for Buffalo’s Week 3 game against the Chargers.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Coleman didn’t practice on either Wednesday or Thursday, but made some movement on Friday by showing up to a practice even if media reporters weren’t truly sure if he was giving a lot of effort. Josh Palmer would be a reasonable FLEX play if Coleman were ruled out.

Source: Katherine Fitzgerald

item.title: Bills coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable and will be a game-time decision for Buffalo’s Week 3 game against the Chargers.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

This is unsurprising based on how the week trended. Moore practiced twice in a non-contact jersey and rested on Thursday. Moore-reliant managers should be prepared to pivot on Sunday morning if need be. Moore did speak to reporters after Brady, giving some optimism that he could be available if he can clear the last few steps of his rehab process.

Source: Katherine Fitzgerald

item.title: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he has “no updates” on when Trey Amos (fibula) will return.
item.description:
Trey Amos WAS Cornerback

The Commanders placed Amos on injured reserve at the end of camp, which will require him to miss at least the first four games of the season. Quinn said Amos’ “speed and on-field work” have been encouraging as of late, but declined to comment on when the 2025 second-rounder could return. The Commanders’ secondary has struggled through the first two weeks of the season, allowing a league-high seven touchdown passes while also ranking 25th in yards per attempt allowed. We’ll have a better sense of when Amos could be in line to return once the team opens his return window.

Source: John Keim

item.title: Browns G Teven Jenkins (back) won’t play in Cleveland’s Week 3 game against the Panthers.
item.description:
Teven Jenkins CLE Guard

He did not practice at any point this week and looks to be questionable for Week 4. The Browns also listed CB Tyson Campbell (hip, ankle) and Grant Delpit (shoulder) as questionable. Browns coach Todd Monken said he’s “hopeful” Campbell and Delpit will go.

item.title: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) is questionable for New England’s Week 3 game against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Eli Raridon NE Tight End

The second-string tight end’s absence may open up more opportunities for New England slot wideout Pop Douglas. The Patriots also ruled out Dre’Mont Jones (shoulder) for Week 3.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: DJ Moore (shoulder) is practicing on Friday.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

He is wearing the red non-contact jersey, however. With a DNP sandwiched between two sessions with the non-contact jersey, Moore is likely to be questionable at best for Week 3. We’ll see how the designations fall later today, but Moore-reliant fantasy managers should have a backup plan ready for Sunday.

Source: Katherine Fitzgerald

item.title: Colts WR Ashton Dulin (ankle) will not play in Indianapolis’ Week 3 game against the Texans.
item.description:
Ashton Dulin IND Wide Receiver

Laquon Treadwell prayer starts are officially on the menu for Week 3.

item.title: Buccaneers ruled out Rueben Bain Jr. (groin) for Week 3 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Rueben Bain TB Outside Linebacker

Head coach Todd Bowles also ruled out LB Josiah Trotter (shoulder) for Sunday’s game. Bain has gotten off to a slow start for the Bucs so far, totaling just one sack while appearing on 76 defensive snaps. The rookie first-rounder will miss at least one game after being sidelined in practice all week. We’ll see if he can get on the field for Week 4’s game against the Packers.

Source: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

item.title: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Xavier Legette (knee) will likely be a game-day decision for Week 3 against the Browns.
item.description:
Xavier Legette CAR Wide Receiver

Legette popped up on Thursday’s injury report as a DNP and was limited on Friday. The third-year receiver underwent an MRI, but it doesn’t sound like it revealed anything too concerning given his practice status for Friday. Even if he is active, Legette isn’t on the fantasy radar this week. He’s managed just two receptions for 64 yards on four targets so far this season.

Source: Carolina Panthers

item.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) is questionable for Week 3 against the Browns.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker is questionable, but it sounds like he’s trending to play after head coach Dave Canales said he expects him to be on the field. Coker was limited in Wednesday and Friday’s practices, which is another good sign for his availability. Through two games, Coker has caught 16 passes for 204 yards and two touchdowns and can be treated as a WR2 this week.

Source: Carolina Panthers

item.title: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Jonathan Allen (knee) will play in Week 3 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Jonathan Allen CIN Defensive Tackle

Allen was a DNP for each of the Bengals’ first two practices but was able to get on the field to close out the week. Allen has been a solid pickup for the Bengals’ revamped defense this season. He’s tallied five tackles while also recording a sack in both games and should have plenty of chances to get after Aaron Rodgers this weekend. Taylor said DT B.J. Hill (Achilles) is doubtful to play this week.

Source: Paul Dehner Jr.

item.title: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Tony Pollard (ankle) will be a full participant in Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

Pollard being upgraded to a full participant on Friday suggests he will be removed from the injury report heading into the weekend. Pollard has rushed 21 times for 99 yards this season while adding another two receptions on three targets. With rain expected in Sunday’s forecast, the Titans could lean heavily on Pollard and the ground game against a Giants team that’s allowing 5.0 yards per carry through two games.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Jalen Coker (ankle) was seen practicing on Friday.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

We’ll get an official status update on Coker shortly, but according to Panthers writer Joe Person, Coker “looked good running routes” during the media portion of practice. Coker was listed as limited during Wednesday’s practice and is dealing with the same ankle injury he played through last week. The fact that he was able to get on the practice field Friday is a good sign for his Week 3 availability against the Browns.

Source: Joseph Person

item.title: Dolphins HC Jeff Hafley said he expects WR Chris Bell (knee) to play in Week 3 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

Bell said Thursday that he expects to play, but Hafley added to that expectation when speaking with the media Friday. The rookie third-rounder has drawn just three targets this season while running 31 routes, but he could see an uptick in targets with Caleb Douglas (ankle) officially ruled out. Bell will be hard to trust as anything more than a WR4 in an offense that currently ranks 30th in total pass attempts and 24th in passing yards.

Source: Barry Jackson

item.title: Dolphins HC Jeff Hafley said Caleb Douglas (ankle) will not play in Week 3 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

Douglas wasn’t able to get on the practice field this week and will officially be sidelined in Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. The rookie receiver has caught seven passes for 110 scoreless yards this season and is second among Dolphins receivers with 10 targets. Rookie Chris Bell (knee) is expected to play and could see a slight increase in targets this week, but this is a tough group of pass-catchers to trust against a solid Chiefs defense.

Source: Barry Jackson

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports 49ers DE Nick Bosa will miss “a few weeks” after pulling his calf in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive End

According to Schefter, the 49ers are deciding whether to place Bosa on injured reserve. The 28-year-old pass-rusher has yet to register a sack in his two games played this season and has tallied two sacks in five games since 2025. It’s just the latest in a string of injuries that has plagued Bosa in recent years. If he lands on injured reserve, the earliest he would be eligible to return is in Week 7 against the Falcons.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Mason Taylor (thumb) will not play in Week 3 against the Lions.
item.description:
Mason Taylor NYJ Tight End

Head coach Aaron Glenn said on Friday morning that Taylor would miss Sunday’s game after being sidelined in practice throughout the week. It was reported on Tuesday that Taylor would be week-to-week with his injury, so it isn’t all to surprising to learn that he will be sidelined for this one. Taylor has -2 yards on two receptions this season and wouldn’t have been on the fantasy radar even if he was active.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: ESPN’s Rich Cimini said it “sounds like there’s some concern” over Adonai Mitchell’s finger injury.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

Mitchell popped up as a limited participant on Thursday’s injury report, and while we don’t have the specifics, Cimini’s report is a bit concerning ahead of Week 3’s game against the Lions. Mitchell popped up for 12 targets in last week’s loss to the Packers and is firmly on the streaming radar against a Lions defense that has struggled out of the gate, but we’ll have to see if he can at least get a questionable tag entering the weekend in order to have any confidence heading into Sunday. Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Mitchell will be limited in Friday’s practice and that the injury came after his finger got caught in a jersey. We should have a better sense of his availability when the team releases its final injury report later in the day.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports Jaxson Dart (knee) will undergo surgery on Friday.
item.description:
Jaxson Dart NYG Quarterback

According to Raanan, the belief is that Dart will have surgery to repair his meniscus and MCL. The second-year quarterback is looking at a 4-6 month recovery period after his surgery, which will sideline him for the remainder of the regular season. Head coach John Harbaugh said earlier in the week that Dart could return in the postseason if Jameis Winston pulls off the unthinkable and leads the G-Men to their first playoff berth since 2022.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Speaking on 106.7 The Fan’s The Sports Junkies, Commanders GM Adam Peters said: “As of right now, surgery is not on the table (for Jayden Daniels), and we have not discussed IR.”
item.description:
Jayden Daniels WAS Quarterback

Peters clarified that this is the plan for Daniels right now, adding that he only recently returned to the team after meeting with several experts. That said, when considering that a stint on the IR would require Daniels to miss at least four games, it would be safe to assume that the team is hoping for a speedy recovery that wouldn’t require him to miss more than three games, putting him on a week-to-week timetable to return. Daniels has already been ruled out for Week 3’s game against the Seahawks and could also be a long shot to play in Week 4’s game against the Colts in London. Daniels will likely wear a brace for the remainder of the season in hopes of stabilizing his elbow, which he first dislocated last season in Week 9. Marcus Mariota will draw the start this week and threw for 1,695-10-7 in 11 games last season.

Source: The Sports Junkies

item.title: Tucker Kraft caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

Kraft has not yet looked himself after recovering from a torn ACL suffered in 2025, this time committing two drops for the first time in his career. To add additional context, Kraft has never had more than three drops in an entire season entering his fourth year in the league. The game plan clearly consisted of getting Kraft involved early to circumvent the offensive line struggles, but the connection with Jordan Love was off throughout. Kraft appears likely to need time to get back to full speed for the Packers, although his snaps and route participation rate were back to normal for the second consecutive week. Fantasy managers are likely forced to ride through the turbulence considering the state of the tight end position throughout the league, but he is a shaky start ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Buccaneers.

item.title: Kaleb Johnson rushed four times for six yards in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons, adding 10 yards on one reception.
item.description:
Kaleb Johnson GB Running Back

The two backs combined for the only eight running back rush attempts on a night the Packers’ offensive line was completely manhandled by an aggressive and athletic Atlanta front. Lloyd took his four carries for 11 yards while Johnson managed only six on his four totes. Both backs were targeted three times through the air, with Johnson going for 10 yards on one reception and Lloyd managing just seven yards on two grabs. This backfield is a complete mess amidst Josh Jacobs’ absence and mounting injuries along the offensive line, with neither back anywhere near a usable fantasy asset ahead of a Week 4 road matchup with the pass-funnel Buccaneers.

item.title: Jordan Love completed 28-of-53 passes for 312 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 35-14, Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
item.description:
Jordan Love GB Quarterback

Love was completely overrun by consistent pressure throughout on a night the Packers attempted 53 passes to just eight running back carries. The Atlanta defensive line took advantage of mounting injuries and ineffective play along the Green Bay offensive line to disrupt any offensive rhythm for the Packers. Love’s two touchdowns went to his top two options through the air in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, the latter of whom notched the first regular season touchdown of his young career late in the fourth quarter. Matt LaFleur, Love, and the rest of the Packers have some significant work to do if they are to save their quickly sinking season. Love falls to a middling QB2 ahead of a road matchup with an aggressive Buccaneers defense in Week 4.

item.title: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
item.description:
Kyle Pitts ATL Tight End

Pitts was the recipient of Michael Penix’s first completion of the 2026 season, with the latter making his season debut following ACL surgery. The return of his starting quarterback was not enough to give Pitts his first fantasy-relevant performance of the season as he watched blocking tight end Austin Hooper score the lone receiving touchdown of the evening from five yards out in the second quarter. Fantasy managers are stuck in the constant hype cycle with Pitts with very little to show for it through three games, making Pitts a difficult start on the road against the Saints in Week 4.

item.title: Drake London caught 9-of-10 targets for 194 yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
item.description:
Drake London ATL Wide Receiver

To make the stat line more impressive, London didn’t catch his first pass until three minutes into the second quarter following a 1-of-5 start from Michael Penix. He would catch his final nine targets on his way to a massive fantasy day, combining with Bijan Robinson to set the NFL record for a wide receiver and running back duo to both go over 150 yards in the same game with three such occurrences. London continues to excel with Penix under center and returns to the WR1 ranks in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 meeting with the Saints.

item.title: Brian Robinson rushed 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

Brian Robinson’s 10 carries paled in comparison to the 29 of Bijan Robinson but were enough to give him his first fantasy-relevant week of the young season. His third quarter score came from seven yards out after Bijan has pulled himself from the game following extensive work on the drive. Brian Robinson remains one of the top pure handcuffs in fantasy circles but will be a difficult start until bye weeks start piling up in Week 5.

item.title: Bijan Robinson rushed 29 times for 194 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Bijan Robinson ATL Running Back

Robinson single-handedly out-gained the Packers in the first half after clearing the century mark on the ground early in the second quarter. His patience and burst through the gap were on full display, routinely gaining chunk yardage on first down while making the Green Bay defensive front look like Swiss cheese. A 55-yard scamper on a wide zone carry in the first quarter got the All Pro back off to a blazing start, adding his first of two touchdowns to cap the drive. He would take on a second score late in the fourth quarter to send the Packers to their first home opener loss in 14 years. Robinson remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the division rival Saints.

item.title: Michael Penix completed 18-of-25 passes for 256 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Falcons’ 35-14, Week 3 win over the Packers.
item.description:
Michael Penix ATL Quarterback

The final stat line looks more impressive when you consider Penix started the game 1-of-5 passing with an interception, settling into the game from there to go on to complete 17 of his final 20 pass attempts. As was the case during his rookie season, Penix leaned on his top option through the air, feeding Drake London 10 targets that the talented receiver parlayed into a gaudy 194 yards, with no other pass-catcher surpassing the 19 yards receiving of running back Bijan Robinson. The Falcons improve to 1-2 on the young season while handing the Packers their first home opener loss in 14 years. Penix has all the look of an upside QB2 and deserves streaming consideration ahead of a road matchup with the Saints in Week 4.

item.title: Commanders RB Kaytron Allen (hip) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Kaytron Allen WAS Running Back

Allen should be good to go for backup duties against the Seahawks in Week 3, although he currently sits in the No. 3 spot. If starting RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt were to miss time, Allen could end up being the team’s lead rusher.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Commanders TE Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Chig Okonkwo WAS Tight End

Okonkwo is on the wrong side of questionable at this point. He sat out in Week 2 and has not yet resumed practicing. Backup TE Ben Sinnott earned just one target last week. He does not need to be rostered.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (quad) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jordan Whittington

It is unclear whether the Rams will get their backup wide receiver back. Whittington cannot be treated as a reliable FLEX starter if he plays in place of WR Puka Nacua (hip) this week.

Source: Los Angeles Rams

item.title: Christian Watson caught 7-of-10 targets for 96 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

Watson now has four touchdowns through three games while ranking one target behind Matthew Golden for the team lead at 29. Even better news for fantasy managers is the fact that we’re likely to see this sudden spike in pass volume continue forward given the current state of the Green Bay backfield and offensive line, meaning fantasy managers can continue to start Watson as a legitimate WR1 ahead of a road meeting with the pass-funnel Buccaneers in Week 4.

item.title: Matthew Golden caught 5-of-12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

It took Golden deep into the fourth quarter of Week 3 of his sophomore campaign to notch his first regular season touchdown, doing so by making a nice adjustment on a ball thrown behind him on a slant in the red zone. Golden leads the Packers with 30 targets through three games and should continue to bring weekly WR3 production, with upside for WR2 output, while operating as the X-type receiver in a Matt LaFleur offense. Increasing those chances is an offensive line that ranks as one of the worst units in the league that is paired with the absence of Josh Jacobs to bring zero run game support to Jordan Love and the Packers, making increased weekly pass volume something we’re likely to see carry forward in the immediate future. Golden is an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the pass-funnel Buccaneers.

item.title: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson should be good to go for the Rams’ Week 3 game against the Broncos. He posted a 6/54/1 receiving line with WR1 Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined last week and could again serve as the Rams’ de facto No. 2 pass-catcher this week.

Source: Los Angeles Rams

item.title: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Cooper Kupp SEA Wide Receiver

Kupp will not be fantasy-relevant in 12-team managed leagues this week, but he could be an option in single-game DFS tournaments. If QB Sam Darnold (glute) can play, he will appreciate having Kupp on the field with him.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Seahawks RB Jadarian Price (chest) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

Price is on track to play in Week 3 against the Commanders, but he remained limited today while receiving specialist, running back George Holani (knee) upgraded to full participation. North-south running back Emanuel Wilson led the team with 21 carries in Week 2. The Seahawks could employ a committee again this week.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Darnold said today that he is “striving” to play in Week 3 against the Commanders. It sounds like his striding is going well, too. The Seahawks’ starting quarterback is now seemingly on track to play on Sunday. Darnold’s strained glute tendon has healed faster than expected. If active, he can be treated as a high-end QB2.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Broncos WR Marvin Mims (foot) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Marvin Mims DEN Wide Receiver

Mims has a chance to return this week, but his availability is not yet guaranteed. Regardless, he is not fantasy-relevant in 12-team leagues. He more so functions as a slight target share problem for other Broncos pass catchers.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: Broncos RB Jonah Coleman (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

The burly rookie has not yet resumed practicing, while both RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) and RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) upgraded to full participation today. Coleman should remain stashed on fantasy football benches.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: Broncos RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

Harvey is on track to return in Week 3 against the Rams after sitting out the Broncos’ Week 2 game against the Jaguars. With RB Jonah Coleman (ankle) ailing, Harvey could take on a slightly larger-than-normal workload, though not enough to treat him as anything higher than a FLEX option.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: Broncos RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
J.K. Dobbins DEN Running Back

Hamstring cramps forced Dobbins to leave the Broncos’ Week 2 game against the Jaguars, but it appears as though his soft tissue is feeling better. A mid-week upgrade to full participation is a great sign for his Week 3 availability. He is an RB2 if active against the Rams.

Source: Parker J. Gabriel

item.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua (hip) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua seems unlikely to play in Week 3 against the Broncos. Rams coach Sean McVay said earlier today that Nacua is “not making great progress,” and his practice participation level reflects that. Rams WR Davante Adams can be treated as a WR1 this week if Nacua is unable to play.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans (hip) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans, 33, can still play on game day, even with very limited practice reps. Reliable veterans do not need the same practice level as youngsters. We likely just need to see him resume practicing tomorrow. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said earlier this week that Evans will “have to be managed this week,” so the current state of things is somewhat unsurprising. If active, Evans can be viewed as a WR2.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Falcons declared QB Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, CB Malcolm Dewalt, CB Robert Longerbeam, EDGE Samson Ebukam and OT Ethan Onianwa inactive for Week 3 against the Packers.
item.description:
Cooper Rush ATL Quarterback

Rush sits ahead of Strand on the depth chart and has been labeled as this evening’s emergency third quarterback. Hopefully, it doesn’t come to that. Week 3 marks QB Michael Penix’s return to action following last year’s season-ending knee injury.

Source: D. Orlando Ledbetter

item.title: Packers declared WR Jayden Reed, RT Zach Bako-Bewele, LG Aaron Banks, DT Warren Brinson and DT Anthony Campbell inactive for Week 3 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Jayden Reed GB Wide Receiver

Reed may not return in 2026, and Bako-Bewele suffered a season-ending knee injury. The Packers will also be without Banks, their starting left guard, though the Falcons are without both starting edge rushers right now due to suspension and injury. Packers DT Javon Hargrave (knee/concussion) is active.

Source: Tom Silverstein

item.title: Eagles RB Will Shipley (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Will Shipley PHI Running Back

Shipley totaled nine touches last week, with RB Saquon Barkley dealing with a stinger. Apparently, he picked up a foot injury along the way. Shipley does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Eagles RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Tank Bigsby PHI Running Back

Earlier this week, Bigsby was a candidate to start in Week 3 against the Bears, with RB Saquon Barkley (stinger) set for an MRI. Barkley’s imaging went well, and he was back at practice in a limited capacity today. Bigsby remains a worthwhile bench stash, but he should no longer be viewed as a Week 3 contributor in fantasy lineups.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: Eagles WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

This is unfortunate. Smith dealt with a hamstring injury back in August, but rehabbed it successfully before the season began. The Eagles have an extra day to rest, with their Week 3 game against the Bears airing as this week’s Monday Night Football game, but he must be treated as questionable to play at this time. Eagles WR Dontayvion Wicks would handle No. 1 wide receiver duties if Smith cannot play.

Source: Zach Berman

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Steelers QB Mason Rudolph and Chiefs QB Justin Fields are potential trade targets for the Giants.
item.description:
Mason Rudolph PIT Quarterback

Rudolph has been discussed as a potential trade target in past seasons, and the Steelers notably kept four quarterbacks on the roster after cut-down day. Fields, we suppose, could be expendable if the Chiefs really like rookie QB Garrett Nussmeier.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Bears QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) is not expected to play in Week 3 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

This isn’t much of an update, but it bears noting. Williams is considered week-to-week at this point. He is not practicing, nor is QB2 Tyson Bagent (concussion). Bagent might have a better chance to play than Williams does, but neither player is on the right side of questionable. Bears QB3 Case Keenum will “likely” start on Monday Night Football against the Eagles in Week 3.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (ribs) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Ladd McConkey LAC Wide Receiver

That makes two full practices for the Chargers’ star wide receiver. Unless he suffers a setback, McConkey will suit up on Sunday to take on the Bills. He was on the field for 24-of-34 passing plays last week, and logged just six snaps outside of that. Hopefully, he can stay on the field for almost all of QB Justin Herbert’s dropbacks this week. McConkey should be in fantasy lineups.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Chargers WR Brenen Thompson (quad) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Brenen Thompson LAC Wide Receiver

The Chargers’ rookie speedster is on the wrong side of questionable. Thompson is not fantasy-relevant on his own, but having him available is a plus for the offense overall. He will likely miss the Chargers’ Week 3 game against the Bills, though.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Chargers LT Rashawn Slater (groin) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Rashawn Slater LAC Tackle

Chargers RG Cole Strange (pec) also upgraded to full participation today. Chargers G/T Trey Pipkins (knee) and LG Kayode Awosika (fibula) remained sidelined. Slate and Strange’s improvements are encouraging, but this unit is still in rough shape. Hopefully, everyone can remain setback-free.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Chiefs DT Chris Jones (calf) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Chris Jones KC Defensive Tackle

Jones should be good to go for Week 3 against the Dolphins, but the calf injury is certainly limiting him. The Chiefs’ D/ST should have a good game, given the Dolphins’ offensive struggles.

Source: Matt McMullen

item.title: Dolphins WR Chris Bell said he will play in Week 3 against the Chiefs despite being limited in practice by fluid and soreness in his knee.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

Bell said the fluid and soreness have been bothering him since Week 1, but he has been pushing through it. The team is now limiting his practice reps so he can spend extra time working with the training staff. As far as how it impacts him, Bell said he has to spend more time warming up than he has in the past to avoid stiffness. Bell tore his ACL in November 2025. He is not yet running a full complement of routes and will likely remain on a snap count, at least in the short term.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Barion Brown NO Wide Receiver

It seems like Brown is very unlikely to play at this point. His agility and long speed define his game as a gadget player and return specialist. His absence could benefit WR2 Devaughn Vele and WR Bryce Lance.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Saints RB Kendre Miller (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Kendre Miller NO Running Back

Illnesses very rarely sideline players on game day, though this is worth tracking. Saints committee leader, RB Travis Etienne, remains limited by a hamstring injury. Saints RB2 Alvin Kamara could log a decent touch count this weekend against the Raiders, though he is a fairly inefficient player at this point.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Travis Etienne NO Running Back

Etienne remains limited, which keeps him in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 3 game against the Raiders. Saints RB3 Kendre Miller was sidelined by an illness, but those rarely impact NFL players’ availability on game day. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara should be rostered wherever he is available.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) remained limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers played through this thumb listing last week and was limited in back-to-back sessions to start the week; he should be considered likely to play against the Patriots.

item.title: Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Trey Hendrickson BAL Outside Linebacker

Hendrickson reportedly broke his finger “into several pieces” last week, yet still managed to record six quarterback pressures and one sack in Week 2. He should play again in Week 3 against the Cowboys in Brazil.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Mason Taylor (thumb) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Mason Taylor NYJ Tight End

He’s considered week-to-week and didn’t practice on either of the first two days of the week. Taylor will likely be ruled out on Friday, opening the door for Kenyon Sadiq to see a workload elevation against the Lions.

item.title: Bears K Cairo Santos (right hip) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Cairo Santos CHI Kicker

The Bears cannot catch a break. If Santos remains sidelined tomorrow, there’s a decent chance the front office will host a free agent tryout.

Source: Chicago Bears

item.title: Jets WR Adonai Mitchell (finger) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

Mitchell was a surprise add to the report on Thursday after practicing in full on Wednesday. It’s a concerning one for the Jets, who figured to build a lot of the passing game around Mitchell, and who have just four healthy wideouts on the roster. We’ll see how this pans out on Friday, but his status is certainly in at least a little jeopardy.

item.title: Bears QB Tyson Bagent (concussion) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Tyson Bagent CHI Quarterback

The Bears’ QB1 Caleb Williams (hamstring) and QB2 Bagent are both sidelined, leaving QB3 Case Keenum to take first-team reps. If Bagent can clear the NFL’s concussion protocol soon, he has a chance to start in Week 3 against the Eagles on Monday Night Football, but Keenum looks like the most likely starter.

Source: Chicago Bears

item.title: Michael Pittman (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Michael Pittman PIT Wide Receiver

It seems like he’s trending towards playing, though Mike McCarthy seemed unsure about it earlier in the week. That’s two straight limited tags for Pittman. Friday will likely determine if he winds up with a questionable tag or not.

item.title: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Jaylen Warren PIT Running Back

He seems well in line to play and, given Rico Dowdle’s second-straight missed practice, could assume the bulk of the load against the Bengals in Week 3. That sentence would have sounded better before Cincinnati reinforced the interior with Dexter Lawrence this offseason.

item.title: Cowboys ruled out LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) for Dallas’ Week 3 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
DeMarvion Overshown DAL Linebacker

No surprise, as he was expected to be ruled out following Wednesday. The Cowboys also ruled out CB Cobie Durant, S Malik Hooker and S P.J. Locke, each of whom are dealing with long-term ailments.

item.title: Bears RB Kyle Monangai (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

Monangai dealt with a knee injury in August that sidelined him for multiple weeks. He logged 12 touches in Week 1, then managed a hamstring injury last week before handling another 12 touches in Week 2. The robust running back will likely be good to go for the Bears’ Week 3 Monday Night Football game against the Eagles, but Monangai’s practice status is worth tracking.

Source: Chicago Bears

item.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

Williams is unable to practice today, as expected. Bears QB3 Case Keenum took first-team reps yesterday, with Williams’ primary backup, QB Tyson Bagent, having been placed in the NFL’s concussion protocol. Bagent did not practice today either. The Bears face the Eagles on Monday night. Keenum is currently the most likely player to get the start this week.

Source: Chicago Bears

item.title: Panthers WR Xavier Legette (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Xavier Legette CAR Wide Receiver

On Monday, Legette told reporters that he was scheduled to undergo an MRI. He practiced fully on Wednesday, so everything seemed to be all good. Evidently, he was not feeling well enough to practice today, though. Legette mostly serves as a distraction for safeties, though he did catch a 55-yard touchdown in Week 2.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Trevor Etienne (ankle) said he will be ready to come off injured reserve before Week 5’s game against the Eagles.
item.description:
Trevor Etienne CAR Running Back

Etienne suffered a high-ankle sprain in the final preseason game. He may return as the nominal No. 2 back behind Chuba Hubbard after Jonathon Brooks was injured in Week 2, giving him non-zero deep-league value.

Source: Joseph Person

item.title: Vikings RB Aaron Jones (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Aaron Jones MIN Running Back

Jones, 31, injured his knee in Week 2 against the Bears and sat out yesterday’s practice. The fact that he is back today puts him on track to play. He will likely be listed as a limited participant, but a full session would be unsurprising. Jones is backed up by rookie RB Demond Claiborne, who would likely handle lead back duties if Jones were to miss time, and receiving specialist RB DeeJay Dallas.

Source: Kevin Seifert

item.title: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that Eagles WR DeVonta Smith “is warming up, but he isn’t in pads” on Thursday.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

It sounds like Smith may end up being listed as a limited participant. We will learn more when the injury report comes out later today. Hopefully, this is just veteran rest as the Eagles gear up for a Week 3 Monday Night Football game against the Bears. Eagles WR Dontayvion Wicks took a hard fall in Week 2 and missed a few plays. He later told reporters that he “will be good.” If Wicks is indeed good and Smith is not, Wicks would operate as the receiving corps’ top option.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is not practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

It puts him in a tenuous spot to play in Week 3’s game against the Giants. Spears will likely need some sort of practice participation on Friday to have a real shot at suiting up after missing each of the first two sessions of the week with this ankle injury.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Titans RB Tony Pollard (ankle) is practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

Pollard could be in line for a boost if he plays and Tyjae Spears sits, as the Titans haven’t really shown much interest in using their other running backs so far. Nicholas Singleton played just six snaps last week. Pollard missed practice Wednesday but seems to be in line to play after today’s session.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Tank Bigsby (undisclosed) is not practicing on Thursday
item.description:
Tank Bigsby PHI Running Back

Journalists have videos of him working out on the side, so this doesn’t necessarily close the door on Bigsby playing on Monday Night, but it’s yet another Waiver Wire Week 3 rug pull possibility. With Saquon Barkley actually practicing, it’s possible Bigsby has zero standalone value this week against the Bears.

Source: Brooks Kubena

item.title: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that Eagles RB Saquon Barkley (stinger) expects to play in Week 3 against the Bears.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Per McLane, Barkley is suited up and present at Thursday’s practice. This puts him on track to face the Bears on Monday Night Football. Barkley underwent an MRI earlier this week. Apparently, the results were good. The Eagles’ No. 1 running back should be good to go, although he may end up logging a limited session to begin the week, as a precaution.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Malik Nabers (shoulder) said his shoulder feels good and x-rays came back with positive results.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers speaking to the media is likely also good news for his availability on Sunday. The 23-year-old wideout is practicing and upgraded to full today, so he’s likely to be good to go and has a chance at avoiding a questionable tag on Friday altogether.

Source: SNY Giants

item.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee) was seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

This is great to see. Bowers has now participated in three consecutive practices, dating back to last week. We do not yet know his participation level. He has been limited in his last two appearances. Bowers is seemingly on track to play in Week 3 against the Saints. Treat him as an elite TE1 if he takes the field on Sunday.

Source: Sam Warren

item.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. said he did not request a trade and said he would play when healthy.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

It sounds like he’s still dealing with back flareups from time-to-time. Overall, it’s an encouraging sign for his availability in Week 3 that he spoke to the media, but Porter admitted that he did not know if he’d be ready to go against the Bengals. He remains questionable heading into Friday’s practice report even after doing everything today.

Source: Mike DeFabo

item.title: Bills DT Ed Oliver (hip) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Ed Oliver BUF Defensive Lineman

Oliver now has a chance to face the Chargers in Week 3, though nothing is certain. The Bills’ star interior defender injured his hip during pre-game warmups last week and was unable to play. The Chargers’ banged-up offensive line has underperformed thus far. This is a situation worth monitoring.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Eli Raridon NE Tight End

Raridon worked off to the side yesterday and ended up being listed as a limited participant. He is not seen with the team again today, so either a light, limited session or a total absence is possible. Either way, Raridon remains firmly in the questionable column, though a second limited session would theoretically put him on track to play in Week 3 against the Jaguars.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) was not spotted at practice on Thursday.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Neither was Keon Coleman. Moore grabbed a limited listing on Wednesday while wearing a non-contact jersey in practice; a downgrade would be troubling for his chances of playing in Week 3. Coleman (ankle) has now missed the first two days of the week and would need a comeback on Friday to get on the questionable line.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Panthers WR Jalen Coker (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker is not wearing a uniform today, so we expect him to be a non-participant on the official injury report, which should come out in less than 90 minutes. We will provide an update if he ends up being listed as limited, or somehow inexplicably full. Coker played through the ankle injury last week, posting an 8/66 receiving line, so we like his odds of suiting up and playing effectively this week. This could just be a rest day. He was limited yesterday. Stay tuned.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Giants LT Andrew Thomas (groin) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

Thomas left the Giants’ Week 2 game against the Rams with a groin injury. He dealt with an ankle injury in practice last week. It is possible that fill-in starter, QB Jameis Winston, will be without his top pass protector in Week 3 against the Titans. Thomas was limited yesterday. It appears as though he will be a DNP today.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Dolphins WR Chris Bell (knee) was seen working off to the side on Thursday.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

According to the Sun Sentinel’s David Furones, Bell mostly worked on the side and went inside before the portion of practice open to the media ended. Bell could end up being listed as a limited participant today, but he is clearly barely participating. It would not be surprising to see a DNP next to his name later today. He was limited yesterday. Bell underwent ACL reconstruction late last year. Hopefully, they are only managing soreness.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

We expect Douglas to be listed as a non-participant today, just like yesterday. Douglas got his ankle rolled up on in Week 2, which is always a concerning injury. Fortunately, his foot was only planted for a moment, so he may have avoided the worst-case scenario. He was later seen wearing a boot. The prudent move is to expect Douglas to miss Week 3. Fellow Dolphins WR Chris Bell (knee) will either be listed as a non-participant or limited, but it sounds like it would be a very light limited, if so.

Source: David Furones

item.title: When asked about Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen, WR coach Chad O’Shea said rookie wide receivers are “always a work in progress.”
item.description:
Cyrus Allen KC Wide Receiver

You don’t say, Chad. Allen was the talk of Chiefs training camp. Beat reporters celebrated his ability to beat man coverage and win over the middle of the field — two aspects that help wide receivers thrive in fantasy. Unfortunately, Allen has logged just four offensive snaps this season. O’Shea adds that Allen is improving every day, both “fundamentally and schematically.” Good for him. The once-intriguing rookie is droppable in 12-team formats, though an in-season breakout remains possible. Theoretically.

Source: Charles Goldman

item.title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Beat reporters observed Flowers working out on his own before practice, but the Ravens’ No. 1 wide receiver headed back inside the building before his teammates took the field. ESPN’s Jamison Hensley wrote, “it’s looking like Baltimore will be without Flowers for a second consecutive game.” The team downplayed Flowers’ Week 1 hamstring aggravation, but he is currently on the wrong side of questionable. The Ravens depart for Brazil this evening and arrive on Friday morning. If Flowers travels, he may have a chance to play, though he will carry re-injury risk.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports, “Judge Marc Hammer denied the request by the victim in the Josh Jacobs case to have the records permanently sealed.”
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

He added that the matter has been turned over to the Hobart/Lawrence police department, which is now in charge of determining whether or not the video will be released. Jacobs or the victim can then appeal that decision. The NFL has been adamant about getting the video before determining Jacobs’ pending suspension, and this increased the odds of that happening. Still, Jacobs could try to prevent that through the appeal process. Jacobs is believed to be facing a 4-6 game suspension, but the NFL can increase the length because of aggravating circumstances. This legal matter is inching toward a resolution, but a clash over the video would likely delay things even further.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Rico Dowdle (toe) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Penn Live’s Nick Farabaugh did note that Dowdle has shed his boot. He injured his toe in Week 2’s loss to the Pats but pushed through the issue in the second half. He was spotted in a boot on Wednesday. It looks like Dowdle will miss Week 3, but shedding the boot this quickly is a good sign that he isn’t dealing with a long-term issue. Jaylen Warren would vault into the RB2 ranks if Dowdle is ruled out before kickoff.

Source: Nick Farabaugh

item.title: Nico Collins (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Nico Collins HOU Wide Receiver

After missing the first two sessions of the week, we fully expect Collins to be ruled out on tomorrow’s run of the injury report. No receiver caught more than three passes with Collins sidelined for Week 2. Dalton Schultz, on the other hand, exploded for 140 yards on 12 grabs and an absurd 14 targets. He is firmly in the TE1 ranks for Week 3 versus the Colts.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Gardner Minshew and Mac Jones as potential trade candidates for the Giants.
item.description:
Gardner Minshew ARI Quarterback

Jaxson Dart will miss the rest of the regular season, though there’s hope he could return for a postseason run.
